paths.title: Databases, Data Modeling & Migrations
paths.description: Design persistent data deliberately so AI-generated features preserve integrity, privacy, performance, and recoverability.

lessons.title: Model entities from domain meaning
lessons.principle: Tables should represent stable concepts, not whatever shape the first UI used.
lessons.practice: Identify entities, ownership, relationships, lifecycle, and invariants before writing schema.

lessons.title: Use database constraints
lessons.principle: Application checks alone are vulnerable to races and alternate code paths.
lessons.practice: Enforce uniqueness, foreign keys, nullability, and valid ranges at the database where appropriate.

lessons.title: Choose keys deliberately
lessons.principle: Identifier design affects references, exposure, and distribution.
lessons.practice: Use stable primary keys and avoid leaking sensitive sequencing when public identifiers matter.

lessons.title: Represent ownership explicitly
lessons.principle: Multi-user data requires a clear security model.
lessons.practice: Store tenant or owner relationships needed for authorization and query scoping.

lessons.title: Normalize before denormalizing
lessons.principle: Duplicated fields create synchronization obligations.
lessons.practice: Start with a clear source of truth and denormalize only for measured performance or product needs.

lessons.title: Index query patterns
lessons.principle: Indexes should follow actual filters, joins, and ordering.
lessons.practice: Use query plans and workload evidence rather than indexing every column.

lessons.title: Understand transaction isolation
lessons.principle: Concurrent operations can observe or overwrite unexpected states.
lessons.practice: Choose locking or isolation based on the invariants the transaction must protect.

lessons.title: Use safe schema migrations
lessons.principle: Breaking schema changes can outpace deployed application versions.
lessons.practice: Prefer expand-migrate-contract and keep old and new code compatible during rollout.

lessons.title: Backfill in bounded batches
lessons.principle: Large data rewrites can lock tables or exhaust resources.
lessons.practice: Batch, throttle, checkpoint, and observe long-running backfills.

lessons.title: Make migrations deterministic
lessons.principle: Environment-dependent migrations are difficult to reproduce.
lessons.practice: Avoid time-sensitive or network-dependent migration logic and keep migration history immutable after release.

lessons.title: Separate schema and seed data
lessons.principle: Reference data and test fixtures have different lifecycle requirements.
lessons.practice: Version production reference data intentionally and keep development seeds safe to rerun.

lessons.title: Protect sensitive fields
lessons.principle: Not every persisted value should be equally accessible.
lessons.practice: Classify personal, credential, financial, and confidential data and minimize collection.

lessons.title: Encrypt where threat models require it
lessons.principle: Encryption is useful only with proper key management and access boundaries.
lessons.practice: Use established platform encryption and rotate keys according to policy.

lessons.title: Define retention and deletion
lessons.principle: Data should not live forever by accident.
lessons.practice: Specify retention periods, account deletion semantics, backups, and legal holds.

lessons.title: Use soft delete carefully
lessons.principle: Soft-deleted rows can leak into queries and remain personally identifiable.
lessons.practice: Use it only when recovery or audit needs justify the ongoing complexity.

lessons.title: Validate backup restoration
lessons.principle: A backup is not proven until it can restore service.
lessons.practice: Test restore procedures and measure recovery time and recovery point objectives.

lessons.title: Monitor query performance
lessons.principle: Generated queries may be correct but operationally expensive.
lessons.practice: Track slow queries, row counts, plans, lock contention, and connection saturation.

lessons.title: Control connection pools
lessons.principle: Too many connections can overwhelm a database.
lessons.practice: Size pools per instance and deployment topology, and release connections promptly.

lessons.title: Avoid production data in local prompts
lessons.principle: Real user data can create privacy and security exposure.
lessons.practice: Use synthetic or properly anonymized datasets for debugging and AI context.

lessons.title: Test migrations both directions operationally
lessons.principle: Schema evolution must work across realistic deploy sequences.
lessons.practice: Validate upgrade, mixed-version operation, data backfill, and rollback or forward-fix strategy.

codeExamples.snippet:
ALTER TABLE account ADD COLUMN display_name_v2 text;
-- deploy compatible code
-- backfill in bounded batches
-- switch reads
-- remove legacy field in a later release

paths.title: Security, Privacy & Threat Modeling
paths.description: Apply secure design and current web-application risk controls to AI-generated software instead of treating security as a final scan.

lessons.title: Threat model important features
lessons.principle: Security starts by understanding assets, actors, trust boundaries, and abuse paths.
lessons.practice: Identify what can be stolen, modified, impersonated, exhausted, or bypassed before implementation.

lessons.title: Enforce least privilege
lessons.principle: Excess permission increases blast radius.
lessons.practice: Give users, services, tokens, and database roles only the access needed for their task.

lessons.title: Prevent broken access control
lessons.principle: Authorization mistakes remain a leading web risk.
lessons.practice: Check permissions server-side for every sensitive object and action, including indirect identifiers.

lessons.title: Secure default configuration
lessons.principle: Development-friendly defaults can be unsafe in production.
lessons.practice: Disable debug exposure, unnecessary services, permissive CORS, and default credentials.

lessons.title: Protect the software supply chain
lessons.principle: Dependencies and build inputs can introduce compromised code.
lessons.practice: Pin important dependencies, review changes, scan advisories, and secure build provenance.

lessons.title: Use approved cryptography
lessons.principle: Custom cryptographic code is difficult to design and review correctly.
lessons.practice: Use established libraries, algorithms, key management, and platform primitives.

lessons.title: Prevent injection
lessons.principle: Untrusted input must not become executable syntax.
lessons.practice: Use parameterized queries, safe APIs, contextual output encoding, and strict command construction.

lessons.title: Design security into workflows
lessons.principle: Security controls bolted on later leave structural gaps.
lessons.practice: Include authorization, sensitive data, abuse resistance, and failure behavior in acceptance criteria.

lessons.title: Harden authentication
lessons.principle: Account takeover risk extends beyond password validation.
lessons.practice: Use proven identity providers or libraries, secure sessions, MFA where appropriate, and safe recovery.

lessons.title: Protect secrets
lessons.principle: Keys and credentials should never be committed or exposed to clients.
lessons.practice: Use secret managers or protected environment injection, rotate leaks, and enable scanning or push protection.

lessons.title: Use secure session cookies
lessons.principle: Browser sessions need transport and script protections.
lessons.practice: Set Secure, HttpOnly, appropriate SameSite, bounded lifetime, and server-side invalidation behavior.

lessons.title: Protect against CSRF where relevant
lessons.principle: Cookie-authenticated state changes can be triggered cross-site.
lessons.practice: Use SameSite protections and CSRF tokens or equivalent defenses for susceptible flows.

lessons.title: Defend against XSS
lessons.principle: Rendering untrusted content into HTML or script contexts can execute attacker code.
lessons.practice: Prefer framework escaping, sanitize rich content, and use a restrictive Content Security Policy.

lessons.title: Validate uploaded files
lessons.principle: File extensions are not trustworthy security boundaries.
lessons.practice: Check size, content type, storage location, processing, access control, and malware risk.

lessons.title: Rate-limit abuse-sensitive actions
lessons.principle: Login, reset, invite, search, and expensive endpoints can be automated maliciously.
lessons.practice: Rate limit by appropriate identities and add abuse monitoring for high-value workflows.

lessons.title: Log security events safely
lessons.principle: Detection requires useful signals without leaking secrets.
lessons.practice: Log authentication, authorization, configuration, and sensitive actions with correlation and redaction.

lessons.title: Fail closed for sensitive decisions
lessons.principle: Exceptional conditions should not accidentally grant access or skip controls.
lessons.practice: Choose safe fallback behavior for permission, verification, payment, and integrity failures.

lessons.title: Minimize personal data
lessons.principle: The safest sensitive data is data you never collect.
lessons.practice: Collect only what the product needs and define retention, deletion, and access rules.

lessons.title: Review AI-generated dependencies
lessons.principle: Models may suggest outdated, typo-squatted, or nonexistent packages.
lessons.practice: Verify package identity, maintenance, license, provenance, and security before installation.

lessons.title: Re-review security after changes
lessons.principle: Security assumptions can break when code evolves.
lessons.practice: Run static analysis, dependency checks, focused tests, and human review on high-risk diffs.

codeExamples.snippet: Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
